items.headline: Nasdaq tumbles and S&P 500 slips Tuesday as Nvidia's rally fades; Dow edges up
items.note: Tuesday's close was mixed after Monday's huge jump: tech and chip stocks led the drop while the Dow rose slightly. Outlets differ on the exact size of the Nasdaq's fall, so the sources are linked rather than a single number. Investors rotated toward older-economy stocks and worried about inflation.

items.headline: Nvidia falls about 6% a day after its 31% surge
items.note: The stock gave back part of Monday's gain as investors asked how much further the AI trade can run, and it is still about 30% below its October record. AMD, Broadcom and Micron fell too, and Micron and SK Hynix each dropped more than 10%.

items.headline: Traders now expect a Fed rate hike in December; PCE inflation data due Wednesday
items.note: Fed funds futures price in a very high chance of a quarter-point hike next month, and NY Fed President John Williams said persistent inflation points toward tighter policy. The 10-year Treasury yield was around 4.9%. Wednesday's PCE report is the last big data point before the meeting, and higher rates tend to hit growth and AI stocks hardest.

items.headline: Anthropic dips below its $83 IPO price
items.note: The stock traded as low as $82.30 early Tuesday, days after its record-breaking debut. New AI-linked listings are swinging with the whole sector.

items.headline: Schumer demands answers on Trump's defense of Nvidia's CEO
items.note: He urged Congress to pass three bipartisan AI-chip and China bills and asked for intelligence committee briefings. Chip export rules could change what Nvidia and others can sell, which matters for the AI industry you want to work in.

items.headline: Retailers jump on earnings: Dick's up nearly 15%, Dollar Tree up over 11%
items.note: Dick's Sporting Goods, Dollar Tree and Best Buy all raised guidance, and Kohl's reported its first positive same-store sales growth in four years. Consumers still appear to be spending, even with the AI-stock swings.

items.headline: US banks' unrealized securities losses rose 50% to $486 billion, FDIC says
items.note: The Q3 jump reflects high bond yields, which push down the value of bonds banks hold. It is a watch item if rates keep rising.

items.headline: Data job postings are recovering but still below the all-jobs average
items.note: An Interview Query analysis of Indeed data says data and analytics postings are up from a year ago but far below pre-pandemic levels, and entry-level hiring is weak. Trackers such as TrueUp count more than 200,000 tech layoffs so far in 2026, so internship applications need to start early.

learn.explain: Sector rotation is when investors sell stocks in one part of the market and buy in another, instead of leaving the market. On Tuesday money moved out of tech and chip stocks, like Nvidia and Micron, and into older-economy companies, and the Dow gained while the Nasdaq fell. The Dow holds only 30 big, mostly traditional companies, so it can rise on a day tech sinks. Rotation often happens when worries change, such as fears that higher interest rates will hurt fast-growing companies.
